Esa última frase es una de las ideas cen: That last sentence is one of the block's central ideas. Two waves with the same list of harmonics and amplitudes sound the same even if their drawing is different, because changing the phases $\varphi_k$ changes the shape and not the spectrum. Joseph Fourier presentó en 1807 la idea: Joseph Fourier presented in 1807 the idea that any periodic function is a sum of sines, in order to solve how heat propagates; the Paris Academy of Sciences took fifteen years to accept it. Georg Ohm, of the electrical law, proposed in 1843 that the ear decomposes sound into those same components, and Hermann von Helmholtz proved it in 1863 with glass resonators tuned to each harmonic. Josiah Gibbs described the corner peaks in 1899, in a letter to the journal Nature, although Henry Wilbraham had already computed them in 1848 without anyone noticing.

The $k = 1$ term is the fundamental, at $f$ hertz: it is the note that is heard. The $k = 2$ one is at $2f$, an octave up; $k = 3$ at $3f$, an octave and a fifth; $k = 4$ at $4f$, two octaves. These are the harmonics. The amplitudes $a_k$, how much each weighs, are the timbre.

Why it sounds like a single note: each harmonic repeats its cycle every $\frac{1}{kf}$ seconds, and therefore also every $\frac{1}{f}$. The whole sum repeats with the fundamental's period, and the ear recognises that period as the pitch.
